docs-architecture-system/components-and-.sent_text: The diagram separates anchor and ledger infrastructure, each with its own node, from application proof construction and terminal verification. A terminal is a lightweight Web2 application with cryptographic capabilities, governed by purpose and risk. Accepted anchor publications supply chain progress without a per-application follower. Verified assets can support transaction construction or off-chain displays and integrations; irreversible effects also need an action policy.

docs-architecture-system/data-and-trust-.sent_text: Ledger providers and Lockness application services are both untrusted for correctness. An application builder may reconstruct state and generate proofs, but the terminal verifies every required claim against the root authenticated through the exact ledger output. Substitute roots, wrong applications, invalid proofs and missing evidence cannot become accepted facts. A builder checking its own inputs does not replace terminal verification.

docs-architecture-system/decisions-00.sent_text: The design reuses generic chain-following capabilities instead of creating an indexer per application. Independent trust remains separate from data provision, and terminals may delegate proof construction without delegating verification.

docs-architecture-system/external-effect.sent_text: An irreversible effect requires a settlement condition as well as verified facts and authorization. A signed root records observation, not future canonicality. Policy defines chain depth or settlement evidence, continued ancestry and refusal or deferral on abandonment or missing evidence. Several anchors agreeing at one point do not replace settlement. The concrete policy remains open.

docs-architecture-system/offload-computa.sent_text: Anchors maintain current commitments and rollback. Ledger providers additionally retain history and query views and serve evidence. These workloads can be operated separately. Follow the trust page for deployment choices and the projects page for the existing CSMT-UTXO machinery and separate cost measurements.

docs-architecture-system/proof-compositi.sent_text: The root-chain diagram starts with a ledger root covering the live UTxO set, then an output and datum carrying the application root, then optional further trees. Every link needs proof and interpretation. A UTxO proof establishes membership, not independent transaction validation. The sequence now starts by discovering retained views, selecting an accepted and available chainpoint and acquiring its session. A refusal stops the read path. The terminal verifies the NFT output, requests an application proof and verifies it against the authenticated root. Ledger proofs stay off-chain; application proofs can enter redeemers.

docs-architecture-system/service-boundar.sent_text: The ledger provider preserves transaction CBOR and required references. Applications interpret the data. History coverage must be specified before sizing the provider. Each endpoint distinguishes authenticated claims from untrusted reconstruction inputs.

docs-architecture-system/why-data-should.sent_text: A proof connects provider data to an independently accepted ledger root at a selected chainpoint. The terminal can replace data providers while preserving its acceptance policy. In the NFT example it checks the output and its datum before checking application evidence. Signatures, ledger proofs and application proofs establish different claims. Real-world effects also require an action and settlement policy.

docs-concepts/a-chain-of-application-roo.sent_text: An authenticated application value may carry another root. Every descendant claim requires a checked proof and the expected interpretation. The architecture owns the root-chain diagram and verification order.

docs-concepts/assets-and-nft-state-outpu.sent_text: An asset identity combines minting policy and asset name. Using it as a unique state identifier requires a policy limiting the asset to one unit and state rules preserving the authoritative output. Inclusion alone proves neither unique supply nor authority. If several candidates are allowed, the application contract must define which is authoritative.

docs-concepts/chainpoints-views-and-sess.sent_text: Chainpoints identify positions, views expose state and sessions retain access under a lease. Follow the session page for refusal, retention and rollback behavior.

docs-concepts/follow-the-example-00.sent_text: Follow the project links into proof composition. CSMT-UTXO supplies the existing engine and measurement starting point. Availability obligations are explained in the market page.

docs-concepts/ledger-and-application-pro.sent_text: Ledger proofs support checking existing indexed ledger facts off-chain. Application proofs support application validation and may enter redeemers. Inclusion alone does not prove query completeness or freshness.

docs-concepts/standard-vocabulary-00.sent_text: Anchors publish independently computed signed ledger roots. Ledger providers serve data and proofs, while application services interpret history and build application proofs. A terminal is a lightweight Web2 application with cryptographic capabilities. It checks assets before enabling transaction construction or off-chain data use. Ledger roots cover generic ledger state; application roots cover application state.

docs-concepts/terminals-lightweight-web2.sent_text: A terminal is a familiar Web2 application with cryptographic capabilities, suitable for a browser, mobile application or conventional service. Its purpose and risk policy select trusted anchors, required claims, freshness and settlement conditions. The diagram follows that policy to a usable chainpoint, then brings untrusted data and proofs together with signed roots from chosen anchors. Verification enables transaction construction or off-chain data consumption; failed checks block verified use. A report or display needs no transaction submission. Irreversible effects require settlement and authorization. Chain following and heavy data work stay with providers, while ordinary application code and verification libraries implement the terminal. Data and roots may arrive in either order, but their bindings must agree and the data provider cannot choose the terminal’s trust policy.

docs-concepts/transaction-cbor-datums-an.sent_text: Transaction CBOR encodes the transaction. Datums carry output-associated application data and redeemers supply script-execution data. Parsing the envelope differs from interpreting Plutus data. The generic service preserves information and applications assign meaning.

docs-concepts/two-roots-with-different-s.sent_text: A ledger root covers the indexed ledger quantities at a chainpoint. An application root is inside the state output datum in this integration. Verify the output first, then use its application root to verify the next claim.

docs-concepts/untrusted-application-serv.sent_text: Application services are untrusted computation providers, just like ledgers. The terminal checks their results against the authenticated application root instead of accepting a service assertion. Follow the trust boundary and delegation story for rejected cases.

docs-design-chainpoints/decisions-00.sent_text: Explicit chainpoint selection replaces mixing latest responses. Bounded views make availability commitments finite, and immutable content allows payloads to be shared across views.

docs-design-chainpoints/find-a-usable-ch.sent_text: Before reading, the terminal intersects accepted anchor publications with the provider’s retained views and history coverage. It selects the network, chainpoint and scheme, then acquires that exact view. Availability may change, so acquisition confirms the lease or refuses. No overlap means wait, switch provider or explicitly select another acceptable point, never mix answers.

docs-design-chainpoints/history-coverage.sent_text: The roots and reconstruction workstream owns history coverage. Choose it before sizing the provider. Declare full-chain or filtered coverage, starting point, backfill, retention, all reference dependencies and refusals. Demonstrate deterministic replay to the authenticated root before cost commitments. Complete transaction CBOR is retained for each covered transaction.

docs-design-chainpoints/open-questions-0.sent_text: Resolve abandoned-branch sessions, leases, atomic view contents, discovery wire formats, history coverage and retry policy. The initial model must expose acquisition, reads, rollback, expiry and eviction.

docs-design-chainpoints/session-contract.sent_text: The state diagram starts with a selected chainpoint and either acquires a retained view or refuses. Active sessions support repeated reads, can expire or close, and can encounter rollback. The rollback branch explicitly has no decided outcome. This is separate from silently rebinding a session. Chainpoint means genesis or slot and block-header hash; the network is separate context.

docs-design-chainpoints/storage-separati.sent_text: The diagram connects a session to retained index roots, content references and immutable bytes. Stored bytes alone do not prove live membership. RocksDB snapshot handles do not survive restart; durable views need a chosen storage design, such as versioned nodes, persisted overlays or database checkpoints. A storage checkpoint is not a Cardano chainpoint.

docs-design-decisions/claims-and-evidenc.sent_text: The root and session model makes a bounded executable contribution to the design. Root acceptance establishes trusted endorsement under explicit observations. Session acquisition preserves the exact selected point for arbitrary providers; it does not establish root trust. Neither provides a full system verifier or deployment. Own and institutional anchors express trust choices, not measured price rankings. Membership alone proves neither uniqueness nor settlement.

docs-design-decisions/evidence-available.sent_text: Pinned Lean proofs and scenarios establish root acceptance and selected point session properties. Observation soundness and honest root correspondence are separate hypotheses. Repeated reads, expiry refusal and release are observable. Removing the actual acquisition guard accepts a newer session and constructively refutes the unchanged guarantee. Branch abandonment and lease policy remain open. Independent acceptance, remote CI, implementation and deployment need distinct revision bound results. Existing MPFS verification and inspected Koios and Blockfrost interfaces remain prior, bounded evidence.

docs-design-decisions/named-deployment-r.sent_text: Anchors and ledgers run nodes. Anchors serve signed roots; ledgers serve data and proofs. Applications serve application proofs. Terminals consume all three, verify them and build transactions or drive real-world effects. The names describe roles rather than a fixed deployment count.

docs-design-decisions/recorded-direction.sent_text: The project treats terminals as lightweight Web2 applications with cryptographic capabilities. Purpose and risk guide verification before transaction construction or off-chain data consumption. The diagram distinguishes design inputs, executable model, reviewed contract and implementation. Own-anchor independence, chosen institutional publications and separately purchased availability remain the trust and economic direction.

docs-design-decisions/what-remains-unpro.sent_text: The root model exposes trusted keys and agreement. Concrete policy selection, key rotation, signed encodings, freshness and rollback notices remain open, together with archive coverage, application bindings and settlement. Coverage must be selected before cost commitments.

docs-design-decisions/words-that-constra.sent_text: The rulings require immutable content separate from chainpoint indexes, independent per-block anchor publication and an API governed by coherent evidence rather than Koios compatibility. Historical CBOR can be untrusted reconstruction material. The preserved present-validity and future-validation ruling distinguishes off-chain ledger membership checks from application proofs used in redeemers.

docs-design-trust-and-availability/desig.sent_text: Separate trust choice from purchased capacity. Offer both independent anchors and institutional publications. Price observable availability instead of treating proofs as uptime guarantees. Require switching evidence instead of assuming an API creates a competitive market.

docs-design-trust-and-availability/evide.sent_text: Follow the decision record for evidence limits. Next specify service and proof contracts, measure anchor and provider costs separately and demonstrate switching.

docs-design-trust-and-availability/switc.sent_text: A switch preserves network, chainpoint, scheme, required claims and anchor policy while acquiring a new provider-local session. Missing coverage must produce refusal. The first run uses two instances of one implementation to demonstrate switching; independent-implementation interoperability requires a second implementation passing the same contract.

docs-design-trust-and-availability/the-p.sent_text: Proofs let data provision become a computational business while terminals keep trust policy. Ordinary capacity can scale through caches and replicas. Interoperability and practical switching are acceptance targets; the decision record owns the evidence boundary.

docs-design-trust-and-availability/two-a.sent_text: An own anchor offers the optimal deal for trust independence. Institutional publications offer an exceptionally attractive operational deal with explicit trust. Both retain software and cryptographic assumptions. Anchors sharing engines, nodes or infrastructure can fail together; agreement is not implementation diversity. The diagram separates root selection from service purchase and combines roots and evidence at terminal verification.

docs-design-trust-and-availability/what-.sent_text: Application operators buy generic ledger services and may separately buy application interpretation and proofs. Availability agreements specify coverage, chainpoint retention, session leases, capacity, latency, uptime, recovery, prices and accounting. Each dimension needs observable behavior. Commercial promises govern delivery; a proof cannot make an unavailable provider answer. Rollback, billing and remedies remain open contracts.

docs-index/current-state-00.sent_text: The project remains at design stage. The decision record owns claims and evidence limits, and the roadmap defines deliverables and acceptance criteria.

docs-index/find-your-path-00.sent_text: Assess trust choices and availability, or start building a terminal by reading the lightweight Web2 application definition. Follow proof composition and chainpoint sessions for the verification flow. Explore the existing projects, evidence and roadmap for delivery status.

docs-index/user-stories-00.sent_text: The terminal selects a chainpoint with an accepted anchor root and an available provider view. In the diagram, ledger and application services remain untrusted. Roots and evidence meet at terminal verification, which enables transactions or off-chain data use. Proof construction can be delegated while verification stays in the lightweight application.

docs-index/web2-scaling-with-explicit-tr.sent_text: Applications buy data and computation while terminals choose anchors and verify answers. This separates correctness trust from capacity and enables competition on availability. An own anchor preserves independence; chosen institutional publications reduce local infrastructure under explicit trust. Follow the canonical trust and availability page.

docs-index/why-terminals-should-consume-.sent_text: Anchored data is data whose required claim has been verified against an independently accepted root. Ledger providers and application services remain untrusted. A ledger proof authenticates an output datum carrying an application root. Follow proof composition for checking further links.

docs-model-index/acquire-the-selected-se.sent_text: The terminal selects a full chainpoint before acquisition. An arbitrary provider can offer any session. The model checks network, slot and block hash, then returns the entire offer unchanged. This proves point coherence and preserves bytes, but does not establish that the offered root was independently accepted. The lifecycle diagram shows acquisition to active or unavailable, repeated active reads, expiry refusal and release to closed. Its abandoned branch path remains unresolved and is omitted from the executable relation. Expiry has no chosen duration or scheduler. The declarations table explains universal acquisition, refusal and transition inversions. The choices table rejects slot only equality, relabelled offers and premature lease policy.

docs-model-index/assess-the-evidence-00.sent_text: The gate builds all modules and inventories every stored theorem, including private proofs. It executes all root and session journeys and the permanent lifecycle check. Deliberate holes and custom escape axioms must reach the relevant rejection. Production root mutations remain checked. The session mutation removes the actual acquisition guard, compiles, accepts a newer session and constructively refutes the unchanged universal statement. The control recompiles the session counterexample and simulator against the mutation, while copying unchanged root dependencies as compiled inputs. It does not rebuild the full dependent closure. The exact unchanged acquisition proof then fails, and the real simulator rejects the changed outcome. These finite controls establish model evidence, without exhaustive mutation coverage. Kernel trust, cryptographic observation soundness and honest root correspondence remain explicit limits. Independent acceptance, remote CI, component implementation and deployment each need separate evidence.

docs-model-index/follow-the-acceptance-b.sent_text: The diagram follows original publications from the selected point through verification observations, distinct keys and trusted membership. Nonempty agreement leads to the accepted root; failure leads to no root at the selected point. Reaching an honest ledger root requires a separate correspondence hypothesis. The decisions table explains why arbitrary observations, exact binding, distinct keys and nonempty endorsement are separate checks.

docs-model-index/read-the-model-contract.sent_text: Shared types preserve exact bytes and the full chainpoint and root identity. Session acquisition and lifecycle now have executable behavior; answer verification remains later work. Signature validity is an arbitrary proposition, with no global instance. Root proofs establish trusted endorsement. Signature validity requires observation soundness; honest root equality separately requires correspondence. Session acquisition assumes neither provider honesty nor root trust.

docs-model-index/run-the-scenarios-00.sent_text: Run the three root journeys and the honest, absent point and newer point session journeys in the pinned Lean environment. Honest session acquisition returns the exact point and the root obtained from independent root acceptance. Two active reads retain it; expiry and release refuse further reads at the original point. Absent and newer offers refuse; alternate network and same slot hash also refuse. Unknown commands and scenarios return usage code sixty four. Source links follow the session feature branch for review before merge; record its head when assessing a candidate.

docs-projects/application-consumers-00.sent_text: MPFS and Singular remain application consumers. The existing MPFS verifier consumes backend facts. Replay from transaction CBOR needs a deterministic interpreter and complete dependencies. The linked acceptance run will test that proposed integration after implementation.

docs-projects/assess-the-evidence-00.sent_text: Use the decision record for evidence boundaries, the roadmap for next demonstrations and the availability page for service commitments.

docs-projects/csmt-utxo-the-existing-eng.sent_text: The linked CSMT-UTXO revision already follows the chain, maintains current UTxO commitments and serves inclusion proofs, historical roots and address lookup. Its documented schema has no transaction archive. The table separates reusable machinery from additional anchor publication work and ledger-provider indexes, archive, retained views, leases and refusals. The packaging choice remains open. Measure the workloads separately; the old CSMT lane stays paused.

docs-roadmap/assign-implementation-work-.sent_text: Assign repositories and deliverables for anchors, ledger providers, applications and terminals after reconciling the earlier epics. Include the experimental archive and retained-view prototype. The terminal deliverable is a lightweight Web2 integration that demonstrates both off-chain data consumption and transaction construction under its evidence and action policy.

docs-roadmap/define-the-acceptance-journ.sent_text: Define acceptance before assigning components. The lightweight Web2 terminal applies its purpose and risk policy, authenticates an NFT output and checks reconstructed state and application claims, including nested roots. Exercise both read-only off-chain use and transaction construction. Two provider instances demonstrate switching. The diagram separates transaction policy from effect settlement and authorization; failed evidence or an abandoned point causes rejection or deferral. Independent implementation interoperability remains a later target.

docs-roadmap/delivery-dependencies-00.sent_text: The dependency diagram now starts with three contracts defining the acceptance journey. Assign components and a measurement prototype against that specification, build them, measure their capacity, then pass the journey before widening the service. An existing CSMT anchor baseline feeds measurement separately. The contracts, Lean model, proofs and simulation belong in Lockness; implementation repositories are assigned before code work.

docs-roadmap/delivery-status-00.sent_text: Lockness-specific implementation has not started. Existing CSMT-UTXO and MPFS provide starting evidence. A product release pipeline awaits a releasable artifact and its owning repository.

docs-roadmap/measure-the-ledger-engine-0.sent_text: Measure two different artifacts. The existing engine supplies a baseline for ingestion, current commitment maintenance and storage, including node cost. New archive, view and session measurements require building the assigned prototype first and showing its reconstruction inputs suffice. Bind results to revisions and workloads, then choose storage and numerical service limits. Measurements do not prove a complete publication service.

docs-roadmap/pass-the-acceptance-journey.sent_text: After components exist, run the defined journey with two separately operated provider instances, unchanged anchor policy and new provider-local sessions. Exercise all failures, nested roots and a chainpoint abandoned before effect settlement. Bind observations to component revisions and distinguish simulated authorization, transaction construction and actual on-chain validation. Independent-implementation interoperability remains a later target.

docs-roadmap/settle-the-chainpoint-contr.sent_text: The Lean model covers discovery, acquisition, reads, expiry, eviction and abandoned branches under explicit cryptographic assumptions. Behavior is distinct from numerical limits. The model enforces declared leases and refusal rules; measurements choose viable windows, durations and concurrency. Reviewed counterexamples must include acquisition races and rollback.

docs-roadmap/specify-roots-reconstructio.sent_text: The roots workstream owns proof claims, encodings, unique NFT state assumptions and nested roots. It also decides reconstruction coverage and reference dependencies before the archive is sized. Publication branch correction and evidence of continued ancestry support an explicit settlement policy. The exit contract names acceptance, deferral and refusal cases. Replay sufficiency is then demonstrated with implemented components.

docs-roadmap/specify-the-trust-and-avail.sent_text: Own-anchor and institutional policies remain separate from purchased capacity. Define observable coverage, compatible evidence, sessions and switching. Usable-view discovery is required; marketplace discovery, billing and remedies are integration choices, with no on-chain marketplace required. Numerical offers follow measurement.

docs-stories-index/act-on-verified-facts.sent_text: A terminal checks data before constructing transactions or authorizing external effects. Ledger proofs stay off-chain; application proofs can enter redeemers. Irreversible effects additionally wait for settlement. An abandoned point or missing settlement evidence causes refusal or deferral.

docs-stories-index/add-an-application-wi.sent_text: An application reconstructs state from transactions and historical inputs. Its result must match the authenticated application root. Missing history is a failure, not an empty successful answer.

docs-stories-index/build-a-lightweight-w.sent_text: An ordinary Web2 application gains cryptographic verification. Its purpose and risk policy guide chainpoint selection and anchor acceptance. It retrieves untrusted asset data and proofs plus independently accepted signed roots, verifies the required claims and lets the user build a transaction or consume data off-chain. A read-only display or report requires no transaction. Wrong points, missing roots and failed proofs cannot be presented as verified data. Irreversible effects also require settlement and authorization.

docs-stories-index/buy-availability-and-.sent_text: An application buys observable coverage, retention, throughput, latency and uptime. It can switch to a compatible provider at the same chainpoint without changing anchor policy, using a new provider-local session. Unavailable views and history must be reported. Fallback must not silently change the root, chainpoint or strength of evidence.

docs-stories-index/delegate-proof-constr.sent_text: The terminal may delegate proof construction to an untrusted application service or construct locally. Either way it checks the required claim against the authenticated application root. Wrong NFTs, substitute roots, invalid proofs and missing evidence must not be accepted. Nested root chains require a separate verified link at each step.

docs-stories-index/evidence-status-00.sent_text: These stories are acceptance targets. No formal model, simulator or production conformance result has yet been delivered.

docs-stories-index/keep-dependent-reads-.sent_text: Reads and pagination remain at one selected state while new blocks arrive. Unavailable and expired chainpoints are refused. Fork behavior remains to be decided.

docs-stories-index/observe-institutional.sent_text: The operator selects institutional anchors under explicit trust policy. The terminal rejects unknown keys, wrong networks, incompatible schemes and stale publications. Follow the trust page for the acceptance requirements.

docs-stories-index/publish-trust-without.sent_text: An anchor computes commitments from a trusted chain feed and signs each block’s publication without serving historical query views. The terminal chooses trusted keys.

docs-stories-index/run-an-anchor-and-buy.sent_text: An operator runs its own node and anchor for maximum trust independence, then buys archive access, retained views and proof generation. The terminal rejects evidence that does not verify against locally established roots. Validation and commitment maintenance remain local responsibilities.

docs-stories-index/verify-before-using-l.sent_text: The terminal accepts a commitment under its own policy and checks the intended NFT state. Changed bytes, identity, root or network must never become accepted facts.

Replacing the data provider must preserve the accepted claim when evidence agrees. A provider cannot substitute its own root for the accepted anchor, and membership alone must not be treated as query completeness.
